title: The logarithm construction and (super) Weyl anomalies
summary: We apply the logarithm construction of higher-derivative conformal primary (super) fields proposed by Butter et al. to derive simple Wess-Zumino actions for: (i) Weyl anomalies in arbitrary even dimensions; (ii) $\mathcal{N} =1$ and $\mathcal{N}=2$ super-Weyl anomalies in four dimensions; and (iii) $(p,q)$ super-Weyl anomalies in two dimensions, with $p,q \leq 2$.

title: The index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators: I
summary: This is the first of a series of papers which will be devoted to a study of the index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on closed Riemannian manifolds. The aim of the series is to discretise the index of the Dirac operator. On flat tori, this is achieved by the Wilson--Dirac operator of lattice gauge theory on a regular lattice. On a general closed Riemannian manifold, however, no regular lattice is available. As an intermediate step between the continuum Dirac operator and its discretisations, we introduce mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on any closed Riemannian manifold, defined by integrating covariant differences over distances comparable to a fixed length scale. In this paper, we define the index of the mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators via spectral flow and prove that it agrees with that of the continuum Dirac operator at all sufficiently small scales. The proof rests on an elliptic estimate uniform in the scale and a Rellich-type compactness theorem. In the second paper, we shall pass from mesoscopic operators to discrete Wilson--Dirac operators.

title: Multi-Channel Non-Abelian Edge Pumping via Multi-Degeneracy Encircling
summary: Non-Abelian operations enable sequence-dependent control of light, yet experimental realizations in wave systems have remained confined to local bulk or same-boundary modes and have often required fragile gap-closing degeneracies. Conventional Thouless pumps, meanwhile, support only two-channel edge transfer across a single gap. Here we demonstrate multi-channel non-Abelian edge pumping on a silicon photonic chip by adiabatically encircling multiple band degeneracies in a multi-gap lattice. In a minimal three-band band-triangle, two opposite-charge Weyl points and one zero-charge degeneracy are linked by global band connectivity, yielding both opposite-boundary and same-boundary edge channels. Sequencing these channels produces non-Abelian braiding of three topologically protected edge modes that reside on distinct physical boundaries. The process remains fully gapped and is protected by topological winding rather than by maintained spectral degeneracies. The same band-triangle principle extends systematically to an arbitrary number of channels, establishing a scalable route to collective, sequence-controlled routing of topological states in integrated photonic circuits.

title: Extensions of the Haldane gap proof: higher dimensions, near degeneracy, fermions and tensor-network states
summary: A recent remarkable paper by OpenAI showed that the spin-one Heisenberg chain with periodic boundary conditions has a spectral gap in the thermodynamic limit. The proof elegantly deduces this gap from the Hamiltonian's spectrum on a finite system. This basic idea is an inequality involving the purity of the original Gibbs state and a dual Gibbs state that is defined via space-time rotation. Here we consider a few generalizations of this purity bootstrap argument. We first extend it to arbitrary spatial dimensions. Our main result uses the space-time duality between symmetry generators and symmetry twists to obtain upper bounds on the splitting of nearly degenerate low-energy states, together with a nonzero gap above them, from finite-system information. As applications, we show that finite-system calculations for the 2+1-D toric code in a field and the 2+1-D transverse-field Ising model establish parameter regimes with four and two low-lying states whose splittings are bounded from above by $e^{-cL}$ and $e^{-cL^2}$ respectively for arbitrarily large system size $L$, while the gap above these states remains nonzero in the thermodynamic limit. Next, we extend it to fermionic systems and use a finite calculation to establish a symmetric mass generation phase in a $2+1$-D fermionic model. Finally, we apply the bootstrap to tensor-network states and establish exponential decay of connected correlations of all local operators in the symmetric square-lattice spin-one state introduced by Jian and Zaletel.

title: Can Two-Point Correlations Determine Gravitational Waves from Sound Waves?
summary: Sound waves are expected to be a dominant source of gravitational waves (GWs) from cosmological first-order phase transitions. Their spectrum is commonly predicted using the fluid velocity two-point correlation function under the Gaussian approximation. However, since the GW source is quadratic in velocity, connected four-point correlations may also contribute to the GW spectrum. Through two analytical toy examples, we demonstrate that velocity two-point correlations alone does not always uniquely determine the GW spectrum. Moving beyond these idealized examples, we investigate a realistic acoustic source based on stochastic bubble nucleation and growth, proving that the connected contribution becomes subleading during subsequent linear acoustic propagation, although cosmic expansion limits this suppression. These results clarify when two-point reconstruction is reliable and how higher-order velocity correlations and the duration of acoustic emission affect GW predictions.

title: Dualities in one-dimensional quantum lattice models: Lie groups, Schur-Weyl duality and symmetry breaking
summary: We present a systematic framework for gauging continuous symmetries, and show that the Schur-Weyl duality arises naturally as a realization of this construction with open boundary conditions. Restricting to compact Lie group symmetries, we construct dual models for one-dimensional quantum lattice models exhibiting those symmetries. We demonstrate that matrix product operators enable the explicit construction of intertwiners between the dual theories and their (non-invertible) symmetries. With closed boundary conditions, we can relate the full spectrum of these dual theories by considering all possible twisted boundary conditions.We illustrate how the Peter-Weyl transform appears when the duality acts on the boundary Hilbert space of a $G$-symmetric model. The presented framework generalizes previous work on dualities for unitary fusion category symmetric models. It exemplifies how dualities for both finite and continuous symmetries rely on the relation between a bond algebra and a representation of the symmetry in the lattice as double centralizers. We argue that dual non-invertible spontaneous symmetry breaking is the mechanism that underlies symmetric tensor network algorithms. We illustrate these results for $U(1)$- and $SU(2)$-symmetric quantum lattice models.

title: Negligible Kitaev interaction in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ revealed by neutron spectroscopy
summary: Using time-of-flight neutron spectroscopy, we have mapped out the magnetic excitations in the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiBr$_2$ over a broad range of energies and momenta. The observed well-defined magnon dispersions are quantitatively reproduced by linear spin-wave theory based on a minimal bilinear Hamiltonian that includes Heisenberg exchange interactions up to third-nearest neighbors, interlayer couplings, and a single-ion anisotropy term, with no need to invoke a Kitaev interaction. This finding is consistent with the fact that bromine is lighter than iodine, leading to weaker ligand-mediated spin-orbit coupling in NiBr2 than in NiI2, and consequently a reduced Kitaev interaction. Our results establish NiBr$_2$ as a Heisenberg-dominated van der Waals antiferromagnet and support the view that the ligand spin-orbit coupling governs the strength of the bond-dependent interactions within the NiX$_2$ (X = halogen) family.

title: Enhancing Gravitational Waves from Global Strings via a First-Order Phase Transition
summary: We perform the first (3+1)-dimensional lattice simulations of a cosmological first-order phase transition (PT) in which true-vacuum bubbles with random phases nucleate, expand, and collide, producing a network of global strings. We find that the string network enters the scaling regime, and the coefficient of the logarithmic growth is smaller than the value obtained for a second-order PT. From the axion spectrum, we derive the dark-matter relic abundance and the dark-radiation bound from big bang nucleosynthesis on the axion decay constant $f_a$ and mass $m_a$. The ratio of the gravitational wave emission rate to the axion emission rate is found to be about two orders of magnitude larger than in the second-order case, and the resulting gravitational wave spectrum can be probed by pulsar timing arrays as well as by space- and ground-based interferometers.

title: Multi-Probe Cosmological Constraints on Clustering DBI Dark Energy Scenario
comment: 38 pages, 19 figures, 8 tables, Welcome constructive comments or suggestions, not only citation requests
summary: We present a multi-probe observational analysis of a clustering tachyonic Dirac-Born-Infeld~(DBI) dark energy model. Its noncanonical kinetic term gives a subluminal sound speed, so dark energy perturbations can grow on subhorizon scales. Working in a multifluid framework that tracks both the background expansion and linear perturbations, we constrain the model with nested sampling, using Planck 2018 compressed CMB distance priors, DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, $fσ_8$ growth data, and three Type Ia supernova compilations: Pantheon$+$, DES-SN5YR, and Union3. The standard cosmological parameters agree with $Λ$CDM within $2σ$, with DBI preferring a slightly lower $H_0$ and higher $Ω_{m0}$, with the largest shift being $\simeq1.8σ$ in $H_0$ for Pantheon$+$. The Bayesian evidence favours DBI in every compilation, moderately for Pantheon$+$ ($Δ\ln\mathcal{Z}\simeq3.4$) and inconclusively for DES-SN5YR and Union3 ($Δ\ln\mathcal{Z}\simeq0.6$-$0.7$). The field thaws naturally. Dark energy perturbations stay several orders of magnitude below matter perturbations, yet the noncanonical sound speed still alters the Hubble friction term, raising $S_8$ by only $\approx0.5σ$ relative to $Λ$CDM. Four independent diagnostics, namely the CPL parametrization, $Om(z)$, the statefinder hierarchy, and the growth index, all point to genuinely evolving dark energy rather than a cosmological constant. The thermal history is left intact, with negligible early dark energy. However, one limitation remains. Because $w_φ=\dotφ^2-1\geq-1$, the phantom regime is out of reach, which is in line with the no-go theorem for a single minimally coupled scalar field, so the model cannot follow the DESI DR2 preference for an effective equation of state crossing $w=-1$.

title: Typical number and stability of equilibria in large non-reciprocal complex systems
summary: We consider a prototypical class of dynamics of $N\gg 1$ degrees of freedom subject to two competing terms, one favoring relaxation to a trivial equilibrium and one taking the form of a Gaussian force field promoting the emergence of many local equilibria. The latter is a non-gradient field, i.e. it includes a non-reciprocal component with a tunable strength. For this model, we compute the quenched complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the typical number of equilibria, resolved by stability index. We compare it with the annealed complexity, i.e. the exponential growth rate of the average number of equilibria. We show that the two coincide only in the fully non-reciprocal limit: for any finite degree of reciprocity, typical realizations contain exponentially fewer equilibria than predicted by the average count. Increasing reciprocity enhances the discrepancy between the two. The quenched complexity depends explicitly on the covariance of the random force field and on the degree of non-reciprocity: the universality observed at the annealed level breaks down. The average counting of equilibria correctly identifies the location of the topology trivialization transition, but it does not capture the typical organization of equilibria near this transition, nor the stability index of the dominant equilibria.

title: Fermi-volume anomaly in quartet condensates
summary: We investigate the relation between density and Fermi volume in a four-component Fermi system with quartet order. For a regular zero-temperature branch without pair order, we express the correction to the Fermi-volume count in terms of the response of the Luttinger-Ward functional to a phase winding of the quartet source. Its leading term is a weighted difference between four-particle and four-hole states. For a Gaussian vertex and parabolic dispersion, we find that the correction expands the Fermi volume in one dimension and contracts it in three dimensions in the parameter range studied. The sign in two dimensions depends on the momentum cutoff. We solve the one-dimensional Dyson equation at fixed density and compare the counting correction obtained from the Fermi points with that evaluated from the dressed spectra at low temperature. At fixed quartet amplitude and peak normalization of the vertex, the correction depends strongly on the vertex width, whereas the fermionic entropy changes little. We also examine the linear pairing response, which can limit the continuation of the unpaired branch to zero temperature.

title: Demystifying Graviton Detection
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures. Extended author version of article published in Physics Today
summary: Detecting single gravitons is possible through the extraction of discrete energy quanta from passing gravitational waves. For decades, this was considered hopeless, with estimates suggesting a detector the size of Jupiter. Here, I explain how these earlier estimates relied on the highly inefficient electron ionization process, while the absorption through the full mass quadrupole of a macroscopic system can bring graviton detection within experimental reach. Operating in the LIGO frequency band solves the challenges of graviton sources and noise suppression, allowing gravitons to be extracted from known passing gravitational waves and detection events to be heralded by classical gravitational-wave observations. Combined with the ability to resolve single energy quanta in macroscopic systems, such as in quantum acoustics, this opens a realistic path toward graviton detection. I also discuss the general limitations of particle detection in establishing an underlying quantum theory, illustrated by an energy-nonconserving semiclassical alternative. Nevertheless, the semiclassical alternative is not standard classical wave physics, and extracting $E=\hbarω$ from a passing wave constitutes bona fide particle detection. This opens the way not only to the first detection of individual gravitons, but also to experimentally probing linearized quantum gravity and the graviton counting statistics of gravitational waves.

title: Testing Gravitationally-Induced-Entanglement with Massive Particles and Quantum Clocks
summary: We present an experimental proposal to test whether gravity can entangle a levitated particle with an array of quantum clocks. By harnessing the collective interaction between a micrometer-scale particle and an array of ultra-precise nuclear clocks, our scheme offers a conceivable path to observing gravitationally mediated entanglement with quantum clocks in the laboratory. Crucially, this setup will probe a genuinely relativistic effect one that requires the contribution of internal clock energy to active gravitational mass and cannot arise from the Newtonian interaction between fixed masses. Therefore, observing this entanglement would provide evidence for the quantised nature of active gravitational mass -- which has not been tested in any prior experiment -- rather than for spatial coherence of fixed masses,which is routinely tested in matterwave interferometers

title: Asymptotic analysis of the dynamical field-field correlation function of the impenetrable Bose gas
comment: 43 pages, 16 figures. Submission to SciPost Physics
summary: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotic behaviour of the two-point correlation function of fields of the impenetrable Bose gas in equilibrium states characterized by a quasi-momentum distribution (or filling fraction). This includes, in particular, the cases of Gibbs and generalized Gibbs ensembles. The overall structure of the asymptotic expansion depends on the number of Fermi points, those points for which the quasi-momentum distribution takes the value $1/2$. The leading asymptotic behaviour is determined by a relaxation rate, a logarithmic correction term and an amplitude for which we provide simple and explicit expressions. In the case of two Fermi points the first sub-leading correction is calculated as well.

title: Initial heat-current decay versus thermal transport at a three-body resonance in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
summary: We theoretically study kinetic relaxation and heat transport in a dilute one-dimensional spinless Fermi gas near a three-body resonance. The full vacuum amplitude of a finite-range interaction enters the linearized Boltzmann collision operator. The resonance position that maximizes the initial heat-current decay rate lies above the one that minimizes the integrated relaxation time. At higher resonance energies, coupling among momentum moments transfers heat-current weight to a slow mode. A faster initial decay can therefore coexist with slower subsequent relaxation and a larger low-frequency heat response. The dissipative responses at two resonance positions reverse their ordering at least twice as frequency increases. Bounds on the full collision operator confirm both reversals. A fourth-moment distortion exhibits the same separation of relaxation scales and provides a probe through the momentum distribution.

title: Primordial non-Gaussianity in warm $k$-inflation with nonminimal derivative coupling
summary: This paper derives the finite-inertia intrinsic thermal bispectrum in potential-free warm $k$-inflation with nonminimal derivative coupling (NMDC). On a fixed Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker geometry, the complete cubic inflaton action determines the nonlinear stochastic source, encompassing temporal, spatial-gradient, and field-dependent kinetic interactions. The retarded solution captures the full momentum-triangle dependence while retaining unequal-time correlations, whereas its equilateral limit yields the intrinsic nonlinearity parameter. The power spectrum is computed with the same response and Gaussian initial state, thereby fixing the statistical normalization. A complementary local freeze-out reduction makes the interaction coefficients and two geometric shape contributions explicit. Comparison along an evolving near-attractor trajectory indicates that unequal-time finite-inertia propagation is crucial for quantitatively predicting the intrinsic bispectrum. The analysis also derives the slow-roll-suppressed nonlinear $δN$ conversion, together with the Arnowitt--Deser--Misner constraints and cubic vertices that characterize the direct gravitational effects of NMDC. These results clarify the respective roles of local freeze-out estimates and finite-inertia stochastic evolution in the nonlinear prediction.

title: The three-dimensional Galilean black hole
summary: We report a novel solution of three-dimensional Galilean Anti-de Sitter gravity. The theory can be formulated as a topological gauge theory invariant under the doubly extended Newton-Hooke group in three dimensions. The solution possesses four conserved charges: energy, angular momentum, spin and rest mass. Interestingly, the magnitude of the spin turns out to bounded from above by the rest mass. The solution exhibits the thermal properties that define a black hole configuration in terms of its gauge theoretical description. Temperature, angular velocity and other chemical potentials are obtained from suitable regularity conditions associated with the topology of the Euclidean continuation of the solution. At zero temperature, an extreme configuration is shown to emerge provided the bound between the spin and the rest mass saturates.

title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $β=2$
summary: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $β=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by Dürr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).

title: Reduced Glass Transition Temperature with Preserved Super-Arrhenius Dynamics in Nanoconfined Glass-Forming Nematic
summary: The molecular dynamics and glass-forming behavior of 4-cyano-3-fluorophenyl 4-butylbenzoate (4CFPB) liquid crystal was investigated by broadband dielectric spectroscopy in anodic aluminum oxide cylindrical nanopores of 35 and 73 nm diameter. The primary $α$-relaxation was analyzed using the Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann (VFT) and Mauro-Yue-Ellison-Gupta-Allan (MYEGA) models. Confinement reduces the glass transition temperature from 217 K in bulk to 208-210 K, while preserving the super-Arrhenius character of the $α$-relaxation and a fragility index of approximately 60. Unlike in previously studied 6 and 8 nm pores, the secondary $β$-relaxation remains detectable, with possible intramolecular contributions examined by density functional theory calculations. Next to the pore-size-dependent changes in molecular dynamics and glass transition temperature, cold crystallization is not observed. These findings highlight the distinct effects of geometrical confinement on molecular relaxation, glass formation, and crystallization kinetics.

title: Exact and Near-Exact Inverse Renormalization Group with Constrained Monte Carlo
summary: We establish conditions for exactness of the inverse renormalization group via constrained Markov processes, a class of Monte Carlo simulations which sample the degrees of freedom within a block on a fine lattice under the constraint that they remain consistent with the corresponding degree of freedom on the coarse lattice according to a forward renormalization group transformation. We show analytically, for an arbitrary transformation, that constrained Markov processes correspond to an exact inversion of the renormalization group at the fixed point action, and to a near-exact inversion in the vicinity of the fixed point. We then optimize renormalization group transformations directly on inversely renormalized configurations to effectively map the action onto itself and ensure computational stability in the generation of configurations for high-dimensional systems. Starting from a set of uncorrelated configurations for the three-dimensional $φ^{4}$ quantum field theory at lattice volume $V=16^{3}$, we invert the renormalization group with constrained Monte Carlo to construct a set of uncorrelated, near-equilibrium configurations for $V=128^{3}$ and extract two critical exponents of the system. The inversion exhibits no critical slowing down, with dynamic critical exponent $z=0.03(2)$.

title: A Simple Approach to the Complexity of Mean Field Ising Spin Glasses
summary: The geometry of spherical spin glasses is relatively well understood, thanks in large part to the Kac-Rice formula. However, this formula does not directly apply to discrete spin systems, and much less is known mathematically about the geometry of Ising spin glasses. In this paper, we present a simple method for counting local optima and gapped states in a broad class of discrete spin glasses. To illustrate its scope, we compute the annealed complexities ("configurational entropies," in the physics language) of mixed Ising spin glasses with potentials, such as external fields, and of the Ghatak-Sherrington model. These computations recover several existing results in the mathematics and physics literature as special cases. We can also compute energy-constrained complexity, finding a critical energy threshold analogous to the spherical case, but for gapped states of pure Ising spin glasses. Finally, we use our method to establish a form of disorder persistence for gapped states, identifying a transition between $3$-spin and $4$-spin glasses.

title: Majorana corner modes and tunable braiding in an altermagnet-superconductor heterostructure
summary: Zeeman fields are usually required for realizing and manipulating Majorana corner modes at the cost of suppressed superconducting pairing. Altermagnetism offers a new route toward realizing Majorana corner modes under zero net external magnetic fields. Here we propose a theoretical scheme to host Majorana corner modes in a honeycomb-lattice altermagnet-superconductor heterostructure. In contrast to previous studies on square lattices, altermagnetism yields distinct effective low-energy edge masses on various inequivalent edges of the honeycomb lattice. Within a low-energy edge-theory framework, we establish the conditions under which Majorana corner modes emerge for both bearded and zigzag edge terminations. We further explicitly construct a complete set of Clifford gates by tuning the altermagnetic anisotropy and chemical potential of the heterostructure. Our results provide a promising platform for the realization and manipulation of Majorana corner modes.

title: An Orbital Curvature for ISCOs
summary: Building on the fact that circular orbits are the fixed points of the phase portraits arising from the geodesic equations on a black hole spacetime, we develop a general orbital geometry, which captures the stability structure of orbits. The construction uses the orbital energy, angular momentum and angular velocity as state space variables, with response functions encoding how the circular orbits react to changes in the black hole background and in their angular motion. The associated scalar curvature provides a geometric diagnostic of certain distinguished points of the circular orbit family, including, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), where it becomes singular. Across the ISCO, the relevant orbital response functions change sign as the system passes from the stable to the unstable circular orbit branch, and typically vanish at marginal stability. We illustrate the framework for Schwarzschild black holes in asymptotically flat four dimensions, and five dimensional Schwarzschild AdS spacetimes. In the four-dimensional case, the ISCO is associated with a degeneration of the energy response sector, while in the five dimensional AdS case it is detected through the angular response. The AdS example also exhibits a separate curvature singularity at a point which coincides with the minimum temperature of the black hole background. These results show that the orbital response geometry provides a unified geometric framework for characterizing the stability of circular orbits and criticality of ISCOs.

title: Space of Geometric Gibbs Measures: Uniqueness, Ergodicity, and Teichmüller Complex Manifold Structure
summary: Building on our previous work, in which geometric Gibbs measures were introduced to complete the space of classical Gibbs measures under the Teichmüller metric, we establish the uniqueness of geometric Gibbs measures in this paper. This result completes the construction of a Teichmüller complex manifold structure on the space of all geometric Gibbs measures. Using the welding technique, we uncover a connection between geometric Gibbs measures and harmonic measures on dynamical quasicircles. This connection allows us to establish asymptotic conformal rigidity for these dynamical quasicircles. Finally, we establish a foundation for the systematic study of the ergodic properties of geometric Gibbs measures.

title: Universal Phase Locking from Slowly Varying Inhomogeneity in Tunnel-Coupled One-Dimensional Condensates
summary: The sine-Gordon model can be experimentally realised by tunnel-coupled one-dimensional Bose condensates. However, the experiments show relaxation to a phase-locked state, which conflicts with the predictions of the homogeneous integrable theory. Here we combine the truncated Wigner approximation with an asymptotic analysis, and show that this locking is produced by a slowly varying density profile through a universal mechanism, whereby the relative phase near the density maximum drifts towards zero. We show that this drift is already present in the linearised theory and its timescale is determined by the density curvature alone, while it is independent of the tunnel coupling. Rescaling time by the relaxation time scale collapses the dynamics for different system sizes and density profiles, while non-linearity suppresses the excitation returning from the edges.

title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
comment: 7 pages + 2 pages of appendices, 8 figures, 2 tables
summary: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model. Our results establish duality defects and generalized symmetries as practical resources for preparing and probing non-local excitations on quantum hardware.

title: Spectral Regimes of Truncated sinc-Power and Pulse-Train Kernels: Edge Exponents, Per-Edge Plunges, and the Landau-Widom Limit
summary: A signal band-limited to one rectangular band and observed through a finite window is the classical concentration problem of Slepian, Landau, Pollak, and Widom. The eigenvalues of the operator cluster near one and near zero, separated by a transition called the plunge. The plunge width grows like the logarithm of the window length, with a universal coefficient of one over pi squared set by the band-edge jump. This paper follows the clusters and the plunge as the band is deformed. An elementwise power of the kernel smooths the band edge, and the plunge gives way to a power-law edge with exponent one less than the power. Disjoint copies of the band widen the plunge in proportion to the number of band edges, as the multiple-interval theorem of Landau and Widom implies, so the coefficient is a per-edge constant. Shrinking each band to a line gives the classical finite-rank operator. Overlapping bands give a multilevel staircase, and a self-similar band gives a cluster hierarchy governed by the Cantor dimension. At the smooth edge, rescaled eigenvalues do not collapse onto one curve. The edge descriptor passes from a constant to an exponent to an integer to a fractal dimension. For the single band, classical results place all eigenfilter zeros on the unit circle, with more of them inside the band as the order rises, so the dominant eigenvectors act as lowpass filters.

title: Ground-state properties of uniaxial magnetic model for antiferromagnetic 1/1 periodic approximants to icosahedral quasicrystals
summary: The ground-state properties of the uniaxial magnetic model in the 1/1 periodic approximant to the icosahedral quasicrystal with antiferromagnetic interactions for the nearest-neighbor bond $J_1$ and the next-nearest-neighbor bond $J_2$ are analyzed theoretically. By performing numerically-exact calculation, we have determined the ground-state phase diagram for the interaction strength $J_2/J_1$ and the magnetic anisotropy defined within the mirror plane reflecting the effect of the crystalline electric field. We have discovered non-collinear magnetic structures, whose magnetic space groups are identified as the antiferromagnetic orders $I_{\rm P}m'\bar{3}'$ and $R_{\rm R}\bar{3}$ with the magnetic propagation vector $(111)$ as well as the antiferromagnetic orders $Im'm'm'$ and $R\bar{3}'$ with the magnetic propagation vector $(000)$ and the ferrimagnetic orders $Im'm'2$, $I2'2'2$, $P2'/m'$, and $P\bar{1}$. By analyzing each ground state with degeneracy, we have revealed the magnetic as well as topological properties, which are useful to analyze experimental observations of rare-earth-based 1/1 approximants considering the effect of magnetic domains.

title: Galois conjugation, droplet growth, and the differential transcendence of the Ising model in nonzero field
summary: The square-lattice Ising model is exactly solvable in zero magnetic field, but the scope of exact solutions at nonzero field remains unresolved. We show that, at every fixed dimensionless field $H=h/(k_BT)\ne 0$, its free energy and magnetization obey no algebraic differential equation in the coupling $K=J/(k_BT)$. This excludes Onsager-type formulas and broad classes of special-function expressions. Previous work left open a countable set of fields with algebraic-integer fugacities. We eliminate these exceptions using Galois conjugation and the large-order growth of droplets of reversed spins. At conjugate fugacities outside the unit circle, nearly square droplets produce coefficient growth incompatible with an algebraic differential equation. We prove that cancellations cannot remove this growth in the full pressure series. The free-energy result also holds for the Lieb lattice and square lattices with equal-length chain decorations and uniform coupling and field. In every dimension $d\ge2$, we additionally resolve fields for which $e^{-2|H|}$ has a real algebraic conjugate greater than one.

title: Polynomial-time classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss
summary: Sampling experiments are a leading approach to demonstrating quantum computational advantage, yet their robustness to experimental noise is not completely understood. We develop a common framework for classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss, including pure loss. For Fock-state boson sampling, Gaussian boson sampling with fixed uniform squeezing, and fermion sampling with magic inputs, we obtain polynomial-time sampling at inverse-polynomial total variation error, for any fixed nonzero overall loss rate, and with high probability over Haar-random interferometers. A milder flatness assumption on the ideal output distribution suffices for quasipolynomial-time simulation without Haar randomness. With constant thermal loss per layer, the same flatness assumption gives polynomial-time simulation at logarithmic depth. Our bounds for Fock-state boson sampling cover both dilute and saturated regimes and become stronger near full input filling: when only a bounded number of input modes are empty, the noisy output for Haar-random interferometers converges, as the number of modes grows, to a distribution independent of the interferometer.

title: Photoinduced switching of orbital-selective Mott states
summary: We investigate light-driven inversion of orbital selectivity in a two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model initially in an orbital-selective Mott phase. Using the matrix-product-state we show that tailored pulse excitations drive interorbital charge transfer that nearly reverses the orbital occupations. Single-particle spectral snapshots exhibit changes consistent with an interchange of the localized and itinerant characters of the orbitals. We analyze the relevant one- and two-photon excitation channels and show that chirping around the lower-frequency resonance enhances the transfer. These results establish a microscopic route to reversing orbital selectivity and accessing long-lived nonequilibrium states in multiorbital systems.

title: Parity-violating scalar-tensor theory revisited: complete basis up to $d=4$ and Hamiltonian analysis
summary: We construct complete bases of parity-violating generally covariant scalar-tensor (GST) and spatially covariant gravity (SCG) monomials up to derivative grade $d=4$. Including all derivative partitions, each description contains one $d=3$ and thirteen $d=4$ linearly independent monomials. At the level of Lagrangians, we find six integration-by-parts relations that reduce polynomial-type Lagrangians to combinations of one $d=3$ and seven $d=4$ monomials with general coefficient functions. We derive the correspondence between the two bases, retaining general coefficients and total derivatives, and establish their independence under integrations by parts. Among the seven $d=4$ SCG monomials, five contain neither the lapse velocity nor the time derivative of the extrinsic curvature. For the two remaining monomials, we perform a Hamiltonian constraint analysis with a standard Einstein-Hilbert kinetic term and a lapse-dependent potential. On the regular branches considered, the lapse-velocity term propagates four degrees of freedom (DOFs), while the extrinsic-curvature-velocity term propagates six DOFs, whether present alone or together with the lapse-velocity term. These results provide a complete basis for constructing parity-violating scalar-tensor theories with three DOFs up to $d=4$ within this setting, with the parity-violating Lagrangian spanned by six GST polynomials: one $d=3$ and five $d=4$ polynomials.

title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
summary: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.

title: Signature of charge-3e tunneling in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
summary: Cooper pairing is a fundamental aspect of superconductivity and results in charge transport with a basic unit of 2e (e is the electron charge). This basic unit can manifest itself as the denominator in the formula for Shapiro steps of ac Josephson effect-nhf/(2e), where h is the Planck constant, f is the ac frequency and n is an integer. Violation of this standard formula may suggest unconventional physics, such as nhf/4e for charge-4e superconductivity. Here, we report discovery of a new sequence of nhf/3e in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions. The microwave frequency/power, temperature, and current annealing dependences of this exotic sequence consistently point to hf/3e as the unit for Shapiro steps, indicating a Josephson tunneling process involving a trio of electrons (3e). This bunching of an odd number of charges distinguishes itself from well-established superconducting processes, which are carried by composite bosons made of an even number of charges. The unusual observations highlight the important interplay between competing charge orders in twisted bilayer systems.

title: Constrained Hamiltonian Formulation of Kinetic Theory for Relativistic Spin-$1/2$ Particles
summary: Describing spin transport away from equilibrium requires a kinetic theory that consistently incorporates spin dynamics and phase space structure. We construct such a collisionless kinetic theory for relativistic spin-$1/2$ particles in external electromagnetic fields using the constrained Hamiltonian formalism. The formulation yields both a covariant kinetic equation and its form in independent physical phase space variables, together with the associated noncanonical Poisson brackets and invariant measure. For massive particles, the interplay between the spin constraints and the electromagnetic field makes the particle velocity generally nonparallel to its kinetic momentum and modifies the momentum and spin evolution. The invariant measure in the reduced phase space obeys an exact Liouville identity even for time-dependent fields. This identity and the equations of motion give local conservation of charge and Boltzmann entropy, as well as balance equations for energy-momentum and total angular momentum. The global equilibrium conditions are consistent with covariant statistical mechanics and the Wigner function approach. The massless construction recovers the standard chiral kinetic equations and phase space measure. This framework provides a consistent Hamiltonian description of spin transport beyond equilibrium.

title: Solvable macroscopic models for populations of type I excitability neurons with Gaussian noise
summary: The dynamics of type I excitability neurons near the bifurcation point are governed by the model of quadratic integrate-and-fire neuron (QIF). The model of QIF subject to white Gaussian noise is abundant in statistical physics, since it not only reasonably reproduces the dynamics of some biological systems but also emerges in the problems of stochastic stability and in quantum mechanics of one-dimensional systems with quenched disorder. We derive the solution for the mean interspike interval of a QIF subject to additive Gaussian noise in terms of analytic functions, from the first passage time problem. On the basis of this solution, we construct analytical expressions for the firing rate and population-mean membrane potential in terms of the real and imaginary parts of a certain universal analytic function. With this function, we generalize theoretical results to heterogeneous populations with Lorentzian-distributed parameters. Implementation of theoretical results is demonstrated and examined for two problems: the interplay between chemical and electrical synapses, and the emergence of effective endogenous noise in sparse inhibitory networks. For the latter case, it is possible to cover the scenarios where the effective noise intensity depends on Lorentzian-distributed parameters, which is not feasible directly with the diffusion approximation.

title: Algorithmic Construction of Vector-Valued Modular Forms and Application to an $A_4\times\mathbb{Z}_4$-invariant Model of Leptons
summary: We present an algorithmic procedure that constructs the Vector-Valued Modular Forms (VVMFs) of finite modular groups, as well as its implementation in a companion code. The usual method consists in building the first few VVMFs, whose tensor products then generate the others. We address the difficulty of systematically finding the minimal set of VVMFs that suffices to produce all higher-weight ones, and we propose a method to identify it that makes use of the Burnside-Brauer theorem. For any given group, whose basic group-theoretic and representation-theoretic description is provided by the user, the code determines the minimal set of VVMFs, explicitly builds it using general results of the theory of such functions, then performs the tensor products that generate any other VVMF. Importantly, it automatically takes into account all caveats that might arise during the study of new groups. Our approach reproduces the known results for the finite modular groups explored in the recent phenomenological literature on modular flavor symmetries, and works for additional groups which we tested. We illustrate our algorithm and the working of our code by studying a model of leptons based on the unexplored finite modular group $A_4\times\mathbb{Z}_4$.

title: Emergent Symmetry in Constant-Density Flocks
summary: In two dimensions, the ordered phase of constant-density flocks is described by a single angle field, which makes them arguably the simplest systems with a scale-free ordered phase of collective motion. We show that the equation governing the corresponding Nambu-Goldstone mode, completed with terms previously discarded, possesses on large scales an invariance combining a shear and a Galilean boost. Broken at the bare level, this symmetry is restored at the unique attractive fixed point, and the associated Ward identities fix the scaling exponents exactly, as confirmed numerically.

title: Nonlinear Interaction and Topological Selection Rules in two Skyrmion Merging: Emergence of Skyrmionium Textures
summary: The nonlinear interaction of closely spaced magnetic skyrmions remains poorly understood, particularly the conditions governing their merger into a single skyrmion or a stable skyrmionium. Here, we investigate the merging dynamics of two Néel skyrmions using analytical modelling and micromagnetic simulations based on Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics. We examine the effects of exchange, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, anisotropy, and magnetostatic energies by varying the initial separation, polarity, winding number, and skyrmion size. Our results reveal a topological selection rule: skyrmions with identical polarity and opposite winding numbers form a stable skyrmionium at intermediate overlap, while all other configurations relax into a single skyrmion. We also identify a critical radius below which the skyrmionium collapses, showing that its formation requires both the appropriate topology and a minimum size. Energy analysis reveals that the transition involves cooperative relaxation of exchange frustration and redistribution of Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and magnetostatic energies, leading to a double-domain-wall structure. The resulting skyrmionium exhibits persistent breathing oscillations around an equilibrium radius, confirming its dynamical stability as a metastable state. These findings establish a predictive framework for controlling skyrmion merging and provide design guidelines for engineering skyrmionium textures in chiral magnetic nanostructures.

title: Signature of chiral anomaly in a graphene-based heterostructure
summary: Chiral anomaly is a fundamental manifestation of topological matter caused by chirality imbalance. It can be of great practical value by providing a mechanism for dissipationless transport. The phenomenon is highly sensitive to the system dimensionality, disappearing in the 2D limit. Different schemes have been proposed to observe the chiral anomaly in graphene-based systems but experimental evidence has been lacking. Here, we synthesized two types of the Gr/Sr/SiC nanostructure - with 2D and 3D, bulk-like, layers of Sr - the difference being the amount of Sr intercalated under graphene. In contrast to the 2D material, 3D Gr/Sr/SiC exhibits a signature of the chiral anomaly - quadratic negative magnetoresistance in parallel magnetic and electric fields. Also, the functional form of the temperature dependence of the magnetoresistance agrees with the chiral anomaly. In addition, the 3D heterostructure exhibits suppressed conductivity and quantum oscillations in graphene. These effects may be associated with the graphene layer incorporated into a complex 3D heterostructure. Hopefully, the discovered signature of chiral anomaly in the built-in graphene would spur research on the phenomenon in topological nanomaterials.

title: Half-integer quantum anomalous Hall effect in MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ via non-magnetic extension
summary: Within an ab-initio approach, we study the electronic structure and Hall response of the antiferromagnetic topological insulator film of MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ in contact with non-magnetic GeBi$_2$Te$_4$ (Bi$_2$Te$_3$) overlayer. The proposed junction design eliminates the exchange splitting one of the Dirac cones of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ (0001) thus manifesting a half-integer quantum anomalous Hall phase. The described recipe allows to enlarge temperature of the effect observation, enriches the diversity of topological properties of the MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ compound and is appropriate for other layered antiferromagnetic topological insulators. Applying the proposed heterostructure design, the half-quantized Hall phase can be established with employing other overlayer and magnetic topological insulator films.

title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
summary: Masked diffusion models generate text by reversing a stochastic masking process. Unlike autoregressive LLMs, which generate text one token at a time, they can reveal many tokens in parallel, at the price of an error, since tokens revealed together are drawn independently. We show that this trade-off maps onto the statistical physics of driven many-particle systems. (i) For any data, the error of parallel generation is the entropy production of the generation process relative to the reversed masking process. (ii) For Markov data, generation is a random sequential adsorption process with labelled gaps, which we solve exactly for any number of steps. (iii) For many steps, the error becomes the dissipation of a slowly driven system: the unmasking schedule plays the role of the driving protocol, the number of steps that of its duration, and the error is set by a thermodynamic metric that we obtain in closed form from the mutual information between tokens. Optimal schedules are geodesics of this metric. The exact solution shows how correlations in the text shape both the error and the quality of the output. The longer the correlations, the more the error concentrates at the start of generation. Schedules that start with small steps then gain more, both in path error and in perplexity, and need fewer steps to reach their asymptotic behaviour.

title: Anisotropic g-tensor and strong spin-orbit interaction of holes in hexagonal germanium nanowires
summary: Hexagonal germanium combines direct-gap optical activity with the low-nuclear-spin environment of a group-IV material, making it a candidate platform for spin qubits and spin-photon interfaces. Using a ten-band $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p}$ model, we study the response of confined hole states in hexagonal germanium nanowires to magnetic and electric fields. We show that, by symmetry, the top valence band of the bulk crystal has a vanishing $g$ factor in the plane perpendicular to the $c$ axis, in analogy with the in-plane $g$ factor of heavy holes in two-dimensional hole gases. In nanowires, confinement induces only small transverse $g$-tensor components, so the $g$ tensor remains strongly anisotropic. A transverse electric field strongly reduces the nanowire band gap, providing a gate-tunable optical signature and limiting the usable field range. The same field induces a Rashba spin-orbit interaction that is markedly stronger for fields perpendicular to the $c$ axis and depends nonlinearly on the field strength. In narrow wires at strong fields, the spin-orbit length reaches a few tens of nanometers, comparable to hole devices in cubic silicon. We identify the microscopic origin of the Rashba coupling as a second-order process mediated by a few intermediate subbands with distinct symmetry selection rules. Our results provide guidance for the design of electrically controlled hole-spin qubits in hexagonal germanium nanowires.

title: Contrasting fate of holes introduced by Fe or In in kagome metal CoSn
summary: CoSn is a kagome metal with well-defined flat bands 0.2 eV below the Fermi level EF. Moving them across EF would offer a rare opportunity to investigate their impact on electronic properties. Using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and X-ray absorption at the Co K-edge, we examine two routes to introduce holes in this compound, through Co/Fe or Sn/In substitutions. Substituting In for Sn produces an almost rigid upward shift of the bands toward EF, as expected for hole doping, whereas substituting Fe for Co leads to an unexpected downward shift. Density functional theory calculations reproduce these opposite trends and trace the unusual behavior of Fe to its local magnetic moment. The moment keeps the hole on the Fe impurity and imposes an attractive electrostatic potential on neighboring Co atoms. Overall, both substitutions bring weakly dispersing states close to EF, the flat bands of the Co kagome lattice upon In substitution and partly localized states around magnetic Fe impurities upon Fe substitution.

title: Non-Perturbative Resolution of Luttinger's Theorem Violations in Strongly Correlated Systems
summary: Many-body physics faces an apparent paradox concerning violations of Luttinger's theorem in strongly correlated systems. The theorem relates the electron number to the Luttinger count -- the monodromy of the logarithm of the imaginary-frequency Green's function $G(iε)$ -- and, at finite magnetic field, connects the Hall conductivity to the magnetic-field derivative of the Luttinger count via the Streda formula. Here, we provide a non-perturbative solution to this paradox. We demonstrate that the reported violations of Luttinger's theorem do not require a breakdown of the skeleton diagram representation of physical quantities, thereby resolving a long-standing point of contention in many-body theory. Furthermore, we show that the Luttinger integral, which accounts for the mismatch between the particle number and the Luttinger count, is itself a genuine topological invariant directly tied to the Luttinger-Ward functional $Φ[G]$ rather than to the Green's function alone. We demonstrate that this invariant, like the monodromy of $\ln G(iε)$ itself, stems exclusively from the zero-frequency discontinuity of the Matsubara trajectory.

title: Pressure-Induced Phase Transition and Superconducting Properties of LiPdH$_2$: A First-Principles Study
summary: We present a detailed first-principles investigation of the superconducting hydride LiPdH$_2$, focusing on the competition between its tetragonal $P4/mmm$ and rhombohedral $R\bar{3}m$ phases. Our results reveal a pressure-induced phase transition near 220 GPa, where $R\bar{3}m$ overtakes $P4/mmm$ in thermodynamic stability. The $R\bar{3}m$ phase is predicted to be superconducting, with $T_{\rm c}$ values of up to 46 K in the harmonic approximation and 28 K at the anharmonic level. In contrast, although the $P4/mmm$ phase is stable up to 200 GPa, it maintains a more rigid electronic character with weaker hydrogen involvement, resulting in lower superconducting performance. Ionic quantum and anharmonic effects play a decisive role in stabilizing $P4/mmm$ and shaping its superconducting properties, whereas these effects diminish rapidly with pressure. These findings highlight the interplay between structural stability, hydrogen orbital activity, and quantum effect in optimizing the superconductivity of hydrogen-based superconductors.

title: Zero-Point Renormalization Reshapes the Shift Current: The Role of Electron-Phonon Coupling
summary: Shift current (SC) drives the bulk photovoltaic effect, holding promise for near-instantaneous, low-dissipation photodetection and energy conversion. The current understanding of SC relies primarily on a single-particle picture, in which the SC is determined purely by band dispersion. While many-body effects from directly excited quasiparticles, such as excitons, magnons and phonons, have been explored, the renormalization of electronic states by quantum virtual-phonon coupling --- inherent in essentially all solids and particularly decisive for transport --- remains unaddressed. Here, using first-principles calculations, we identify this missing channel --- band-renormalized shift current (BRSC) --- in monolayer MoS2. We find that the zero-point renormalization alone, without any polarization-carrying photoexcited phonons and with barely any alteration of the band dispersion, dramatically reshapes the SC spectrum: emergent low-energy peaks arise from phonon-assisted optical transitions between momentum-distinct states, with a pronounced redshift of higher-energy features. A mere 1.0% strain sharply tunes the BRSC, whereas raising the temperature enhances it. Our findings overturn the band-structure-only paradigm, establishing electron-phonon coupling as an indispensable ingredient for nonlinear photocurrent and opening a strain-thermal route for engineering next-generation optoelectronic responses.

title: Heat Transport Mechanisms in MOF-5
summary: We find that MOF-5 supports both long-lived phonons and linker vibrations whose split spectra signal a breakdown of the phonon quasiparticle approximation. Combining mode-projected molecular dynamics spectra with spectral Wigner heat transport, we resolve two contrasting transport channels: low-frequency particle-like phonon propagation decreases strongly from 200 to 500 K, whereas wave-like phonon coherence remains nearly constant and supplies about half the intrinsic conductivity at 500 K. A phenomenological extrinsic scattering model provides a plausible explanation for the discrepancy between calculated and measured conductivities in terms of both its magnitude and temperature dependence. We also identify signatures of phonon quasiparticle breakdown in the linker vibrations of ZIF-8 and HKUST-1, indicating that this feature extends to other metal-organic frameworks.

title: Splay ostracism on ferroelectric nematic shells
summary: Ostracism was the practice in use in Athens and other ancient Greek cities to send into exile citizens whose influence was deemed to be dangerous. Quite similarly, splay ostracism is here the approximation that bans splay distortion from thin films of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals on a curved shell in space. This reduces to a mere geometric problem the quest for equilibria of director vortexes and the walls isolating them, as splay ostracism requires the director field lines to be everywhere orthogonal to systems of geodesics on the shell. Consequences of this theorem are explored for shells with Gaussian curvature of either sign. The resulting quasi static dynamics reveals both cases where walls escape from the shell and cases where they are trapped on it, with possibly different reflections on the vortex dynamics.

title: Microscopic Origin and Josephson Signatures of $d$-Wave Superconductivity in Monolayer FeSe
summary: Monolayer FeSe on SrTiO$_3$ exhibits high-temperature superconductivity with an electron-only Fermi surface, raising fundamental questions about its unconventional pairing mechanism. Motivated by recent Josephson scanning tunneling microscopy evidence for nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity, we investigate the microscopic role of the Fe $d_{xy}$ orbital using an experimentally constrained multiorbital theory. A tight-binding model fitted to quasiparticle interference and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals substantial $d_{xy}$ character near the Fermi level and dominant nearest-neighbor hopping, in contrast to the conventional kinetic-frustration picture of iron-based superconductors. Both itinerant spin-fluctuation calculations and strong-coupling exchange approaches favor a robust $d$-wave pairing state, whose interband pairing components allow a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum. We further establish a symmetry-based selection rule for spatial Josephson tunneling, revealing characteristic bond-centered maxima and mirror-enforced interference zeros that distinguish $d$-wave pairing from competing $s$-wave states. These symmetry-enforced nodal lines survive near Fe-site impurities, while a pronounced contrast between the $d$- and $s$-wave Josephson patterns persists around vortices despite the loss of mirror protection. Our results connect the unconventional $d_{xy}$ electronic structure to nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity and demonstrate the power of spatial Josephson interference for resolving pairing symmetry in multiorbital superconductors.

title: When Molecular Dimerization Induces Magnetic Bi-Stability at the Metal-Organic Interface
summary: We present a method to create metal-organic dimer complexes by on-surface assembly on a metal substrate using low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS). We demonstrate that a dimer of Mn-Phthalocyanine (MnPc)2 on a Ag(111) surface can be switched between two stable configurations upon a small conformational change controlled by STM manipulation. By means of density-functional theory calculations, it is found that the two conformations correspond to an antiferromagnetic (AFM) and a ferromagnetic (FM) state respectively. Directly coordinated Mn atoms of the dimer lead to an AFM-coupling whereas indirectly coordinated (shifted) Mn atoms lead to a FM-coupling. Rarely seen in a molecular- dimers with transition-metal atoms, the FM-AFM-FM transition is thus readily on-surface accessible. Furthermore, the two configurations of the switch are easily identified by their Kondo states, opening interesting routes in terms of both, writing (FM versus AFM states) and reading. These results pave the experimental route toward dimer-based materials with complex magnetic structures of potential interest for application in spintronics, logics and computing.

title: Closed-form solution for semi-symmetric folding of waterbomb tessellations
comment: Accepted for publication in Proceedings of the Royal Society A. 24 pages. Author accepted manuscript
summary: Rigid-origami folding has versatile applications in the fields of architecture, engineering, medicine and aerospace. Given the design parameters of a single waterbomb cell, the global geometry of the origami tessellated shell at an intermediate state of folding is directly determined. Even though existing numerical methods of rigid-origami can be used to describe geometric forms, algebraic solutions of the waterbomb folding kinematics and tessellations reduce the algorithmic complexity and determine the range of admissible configurations exactly. The existing analytical solution for a symmetrically folded waterbomb cell and tessellation is extended to the case of a cell folded semi-symmetrically, i.e. a cell with a 180° rotation symmetry. The algebraic derivation provides the solution for the entire folding process. The resulting functional relationship between the design parameters and the 3D cell geometry of the folded waterbomb cell enables efficient studies of achievable shell geometries. This development facilitates a deeper understanding of the correspondence between the geometric parameters of a single waterbomb cell and the statically relevant geometric properties, i.e. the shell curvature and the effective cross-sectional height. The systematic description of this correspondence provides the basis for innovative design concepts using modern cementitious composites, e.g. textile-reinforced concrete, to produce thin-walled, high-performance, lightweight shells.

title: First-order condensation and meniscus pinning in finite open wedges
summary: We study first-order condensation in finite open wedges using classical density functional theory (DFT) and compare the resulting microscopic phase behaviour with recent macroscopic predictions. Two geometries are considered: a symmetric wedge formed by two identical inclined walls and an asymmetric wedge formed by a vertical and an inclined wall. The DFT calculations confirm the two condensed morphologies predicted for the symmetric wedge and the three morphologies predicted for the asymmetric wedge and their emergence depending on the wedge size, opening angle, and wall contact angle. Under partial-wetting conditions, the microscopic phase boundaries are in nearly perfect quantitative agreement with the macroscopic predictions, including reentrant changes between pinned and depinned meniscus configurations and the appearance of the semi-double-pinned state in the asymmetric wedge. Under complete-wetting conditions, the DFT phase diagrams retain the topology predicted by the macroscopic theory, but the single-pinned region is systematically enlarged. This shift is attributed to adsorbed liquid films, which reduce the effective width available to the gas and thereby increase the effective aspect ratio of the confinement.

title: Ferroelectric control of magnetic coupling in a Cr dimer adsorbed on $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$
summary: Ferroelectric substrates offer a route to controlling magnetic interactions in low-dimensional systems through polarization-dependent changes in local bonding and electronic structure. Here, using first-principles calculations, we investigate the adsorption of 3$d$ transition-metal atoms and dimers on monolayer $α$-In$_2$Se$_3$ and identify Cr as a stable dimer configuration on both polar surfaces. Reversing the ferroelectric polarization drives a pronounced change in its magnetic coupling: the AFM state is favored for one polarization, whereas the FM and AFM configurations become nearly degenerate for the opposite one. Analysis of the spin density, projected electronic states, and Wannier Hamiltonians reveals concomitant changes in the direct Cr-Cr hopping and in the interaction with the bridging Se atom. In particular, enhanced Cr-Se hybridization and Se spin polarization, together with a strong reduction of the direct two-center Cr-Cr hopping, point to a polarization-dependent balance between direct and substrate-mediated exchange contributions. These results show how ferroelectric polarization can tune magnetic interactions in an atomically defined 2D hybrid system.

title: Key role of orbital exchange in CoO magnetism
summary: Co ions in the antiferromagnetic phase of CoO are known to possess a substantial orbital moment, making this material promising for orbitronic applications. However, intersite exchange interactions involving these orbital degrees of freedom remain poorly quantified, and their role in CoO magnetism is unclear. Here, we derive a full low-energy effective Hamiltonian for CoO, including orbital exchange terms, using an ab initio force-theorem approach based on DFT+dynamical mean-field theory. We find sizable orbital interactions, with quadrupolar orbital exchange emerging as the dominant nearest-neighbor term. The collinear antiferromagnetic order obtained from the effective Hamiltonian features magnetic moments tilted away from the pseudocubic <001> direction and an orbital contribution amounting to about one-third of the total moment, in agreement with experimental estimates. We show that the moment tilting originates from the combined effect of orbital and spin-orbital exchange interactions. The same interactions also produce a prominent splitting of the lowest excitation band. By directly modeling the inelastic neutron scattering (INS) intensity, we further show that the characteristic column-like structures previously observed in CoO INS provide a clear fingerprint of orbital exchange. We also discuss possible impact of our findings for further advances in the field of complex collective excitations, their transport properties and applications in the realm of orbitronics.

title: The polar discontinuity picture in nickelate superlattices: comparison of the insulating and metallic phases
summary: We present a first-principles study of the formal-charge polar discontinuity in superlattices of BaTiO$_3$ interfaced with SmNiO$_3$ or BiNiO$_3$, comparing the results for the insulating and metallic nickelate phases. Polar discontinuities arising from differently charged layers in perovskites are well-studied in heterostructures such as LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$, and recently, signatures consistent with such a polar discontinuity have been observed in systems where the formally charged layers would reside in a metal. We first identify signatures of the polar discontinuity in the structure and the density of states of superlattices with BaTiO$_3$ and insulating BiNiO$_3$, and find partial screening by modification of the BiNiO$_3$ charge disproportionation pattern analogous to our previous study on BaTiO$_3$/SmNiO$_3$. We then examine superlattices constructed from the corresponding metallic nickelate phases and find that, despite the presence of screening charges, the qualitative interfacial response is remarkably similar to that of the insulating counterparts. We show that the metallic screening charges have little influence on the apparent formal-charge polar discontinuity and discuss practical limitations of the polar-discontinuity picture when interpreting and quantifying screening at metallic nickelate/ferroelectric interfaces.

title: Thermodynamic geometry of three coupled Ising spins: exact curvature, frustration and bond anisotropy
summary: Thermodynamic curvature is widely used as a diagnostic of interactions and phase transitions, yet its interpretation is usually tested only in the thermodynamic limit. Small spin clusters are physically relevant in their own right, since a macroscopic sample of independent molecular trimers or a few-qubit quantum simulator is governed exactly by the few-spin partition function. They also provide the only setting in which the geometry can be obtained in closed form together with its full dependence on the interaction topology. We study the Fisher-Rao (Ruppeiner) geometry of three Ising spins with arbitrary pairwise couplings in a longitudinal field. This cluster interpolates continuously between an open chain and a geometrically frustrated triangle. For the symmetric triangle we obtain the scalar curvature in closed form. It vanishes on the noninteracting line and on a line of fixed field-to-temperature ratio that does not depend on the coupling, which coincides with the inflection point of the single-spin susceptibility. The near-zero behaviour is therefore exactly linear and reflects analyticity rather than critical scaling. In the frustrated antiferromagnetic regime the curvature remains finite and negative down to zero temperature. A general low-temperature formula relates this plateau to the change in magnetization content between the degenerate ground manifold and its first excitation. Any bond anisotropy destroys the plateau below a crossover temperature that depends only logarithmically on the anisotropy, so the curvature is an extremely sensitive detector of exact ground-state degeneracy. On the ferromagnetic side the zero-temperature curvature is universal for all couplings, whereas additional zero lines in anisotropic clusters track field-induced crossings of excited levels.

title: Coherent phase slips in coupled rings: from weak to strong interactions
summary: We study the coherent transfer of circulation between two weakly coupled lattice rings of ultracold bosons, in which a persistent current initially prepared in one ring oscillates back and forth between the rings without net transfer of particles. Combining Bose--Hubbard simulations with their Gross--Pitaevskii and quantum phase model limits, we show that similar current oscillations arise from two distinct microscopic mechanisms. At weak interactions, particles in each occupied momentum mode tunnel independently between the rings, leading to a transfer time inversely proportional to the inter-ring tunnelling, extensive particle-number fluctuations and entanglement distributed over many Schmidt components; this mode-exchange dynamics is suppressed by self-trapping as the interactions increase. At stronger interactions and large filling, in the phase-dominated regime, circulation is instead transferred through a second-order collective process between many-body persistent-current states, with a transfer time scaling as the inverse square of the inter-ring tunnelling in the weak-link limit. Number fluctuations then remain of order one instead of growing with the particle number, and within each number sector the system evolves into coherent superpositions of two many-body configurations, distinguished by which ring carries the circulation. The entanglement accessible under number-conserving operations therefore reaches up to approximately one bit. We propose a quench protocol to prepare the initial state and estimate transfer times within reach of current ring-lattice experiments, identifying coupled rings as a platform to study coherent quantum phase slips and to manipulate persistent-current states.

title: Hydrodynamic interaction in Lattice Fokker Planck for dilute polymer dynamics
summary: We extend the BGK-type kinetic model for polymer dumbbells and its lattice Boltzmann implementation by incorporating hydrodynamic interaction (HI) effects to accurately recover the slow-variable dynamics governed by the Smoluchowski equation. Unlike Brownian dynamics approaches, which demand the computationally expensive evaluation of the square root of the configuration-dependent diffusion tensor at every time step, this kinetic method is straightforward to implement and avoids such overhead entirely. Consequently, it achieves a significant reduction in computational cost. We validate the model in steady and transient shear flows, demonstrating its ability to capture the distinct signatures of hydrodynamic interactions on bulk rheological properties.

title: Experimental Evidence for Type-I Superconductivity in $\mathrm{OsB_2}$
summary: Since the discovery of superconductivity in $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, metal diborides have attracted significant attention. Among these, osmium diboride ($\mathrm{OsB_2}$), crystallizing in an orthorhombic structure (space group $Pmmn$) with puckered boron layers, has been classified as a low-$κ$ Type-II superconductor ($T_c \approx 2.1~\mathrm{K}$). Here, we report experimental evidence establishing that $\mathrm{OsB_2}$ is in fact a rare nonelemental Type-I superconductor. Our identification is supported by three primary experimental hallmarks: (i) a pronounced Differential Paramagnetic Effect (DPE) peak in AC susceptibility ($χ_{ac}$) measurements under static DC magnetic fields, signaling the intermediate state; (ii) a field-induced crossover to a divergent first-order phase transition in specific heat ($C/T$); and (iii) pronounced magnetic hysteresis in field-ramped transitions indicative of supercooling.

title: Finite-element reconstruction of molten-zone dynamics and chemical segregation in optical floating-zone grown Ni--Mn--Ga
summary: Homogeneous single-crystal growth of Ni--Mn--Ga magnetic shape-memory alloys is limited by incongruent melting, Mn reactivity, and longitudinal composition segregation. We report a modified optical floating-zone method in which growth is performed inside a transparent sapphire crucible, stabilising the molten zone while preserving optical heating and visual monitoring. The resulting crystals show improved growth reproducibility and controlled macroscopic geometry. To interpret the measured segregation profiles, a transient finite-element heat-transfer model in COMSOL Multiphysics was coupled to an effective molten-zone mass-balance calculation. The model reveals that the local solidification velocity is not fixed by the imposed translation speed but varies strongly as the molten-zone geometry evolves. The calculated solidification-front geometry is independently supported by EBSD analysis of a quenched growth interface, while the coupled mass-balance calculation reproduces the dominant features of the measured composition profiles. These results show that deviations from ideal Scheil--Pfann behaviour arise from the evolving molten-zone geometry and solidification conditions. The experimentally constrained model therefore provides a practical means of reconstructing otherwise inaccessible growth conditions and a basis for optimisation of sapphire-confined floating-zone growth of incongruently melting alloys.

title: Thermodynamics of Forgetting in a Bounded Hopfield Network
summary: A memory that keeps learning must also forget. The Hopfield network does not: beyond a critical number of stored patterns it falls into a state of total confusion and retrieves none of them. Parisi showed in 1986 that bounding the synaptic strength cures this pathology, since the clipping of the couplings gradually erases the oldest memories and leaves room for the new ones. In this paper we provide a thermodynamic description of the resulting network, known as the Hopfield-Parisi model. Starting from the learning rule, we show that the network is equivalent to a Hopfield model whose patterns are weighted according to their age, superimposed on a Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, both governed by the synaptic bound: a larger bound makes the memory longer, but also noisier. The theory of nonlinear networks developed in the eighties already provides, through the heuristic replica method, the equations that govern this model at any temperature, but to the best of our knowledge they have been solved only at zero temperature. We rederive them at the replica symmetric level through Guerra's interpolation and solve them at finite temperature, obtaining the phase diagram of the model together with its memory horizon, namely the largest age at which a pattern can still be retrieved. The solution shows that forgetting acts on the signal alone, the noise being the same for patterns of every age, and that the horizon is maximal at an intermediate bound which is essentially insensitive to temperature. Monte Carlo simulations of networks trained with the original learning rule support these predictions.

title: Spin supersolid in triangular lattice easy-axis spin-1/2 antiferromagnet: a fermionic parton perspective
summary: We study the supersolid order of the spin-1/2 easy-axis XXZ antiferromagnet on the triangular lattice using a fermionic parton mean-field theory built on the $π$-flux Dirac spin liquid, with the mean-field order generated by an on-site spinon interaction term and nearest-neighbor (anisotropic) spin couplings. The collective modes are obtained using the random-phase approximation (RPA). In a finite parameter region, we find the Y state as a self-consistent solution, together with the competing Y' state, which is a $90^\circ$-rotated Y state inside the order plane. The mean-field energy favors Y', even though the two states are exactly degenerate in the classical limit. However, the Y state can become lower in energy when higher-order corrections due to the fluctuations of the collective modes are considered. The Y state can also be stabilized on the mean-field level by applying small external fields, which we do in two different ways: moment-aligned local field and uniform field along the easy axis. In both cases, the RPA calculation for the stabilized Y state gives a roton minimum at the $M$ point in the excitation spectrum. A gapped pseudo-Goldstone mode above the gapless Goldstone mode is obtained as well, which has also been observed experimentally. Furthermore, we investigate the effects of tuning the spinon interaction strength and the anisotropy in spin couplings in our phenomenological model. Comparison with the recent numerical and experimental results is also discussed.

title: Dynamical Keldysh model for colored noise and finite relaxation rate
summary: The Keldysh model describes quantum dots subjected to Gaussian noise with infinite correlation time.
